summary: Source decomposition of the PEL moduli roadmap from Kai-Wen Lan's revised thesis 'Arithmetic compactifications of PEL-type Shimura varieties' (revision of March 14, 2021): Chapter 1 read in full and Chapter 2 read with all proofs of Sections 2.2-2.3 and the parts of 2.1 they use, plus the Artin-criterion theorems of Appendix B. M0 transcribes the linear algebra: discriminants and unramified primes, the determinant polynomial classifying modules in every characteristic (with the trace criterion confined to characteristic zero), multiranks, PEL-type O-lattices and the similitude group scheme, the Albert types with I_bad, torsion-freeness of universal domains, the standard form of self-dual symplectic modules at primes not dividing I_bad Disc, smoothness of G, Gram-Schmidt lifting, the reflex field F_0, integrality of Det over O_{F_0}, and formal smoothness of G/P_0 at primes not dividing I_bad Disc [L^#:L]. M1 transcribes the moduli problems: quasi-isogenies, polarizations, Rosati-compatible O-structures, the Kottwitz determinantal condition, symplectic-liftable level structures, rational level structures, M_H by isomorphism classes over O_{F_0,(box)} for a set box of good primes, M^rat_H by Z_(box)^x-isogeny classes, their comparison (Prop. 1.4.3.4), the etale stack property, and changes of lattice and of box. M2 transcribes the proof of Theorem 1.4.1.11 (separated smooth algebraic stack of finite type, algebraic space at neat level) through obstruction theory, the de Rham lifting criterion, Schlessinger prorepresentability, formal smoothness with dimension dim_C Sym(V_0), Grothendieck existence, level-n rigidity and Artin's criterion, plus the Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism. M3-M5 use Lan's example-based introduction (Section 5.1), Milne's Introduction to Shimura varieties (Sections 6-8, 12, 14) and Hida's p-adic automorphic forms on reductive groups (Sections 5.2, 6.1-6.2) for the complex points, the failure of the Hasse principle, canonical models and examples; the actual comparison theorems there are cited to Kottwitz (JAMS 1992) and Lan (Crelle 2012), both absent from the library, and are recorded as gaps. M6 records the level-n rigidity export used in the descent step of Faltings' Satz 1. Imports that were not read (Reiner, Mumford, Berthelot-Breen-Messing, SGA 1, EGA, Artin, Schlessinger, Kottwitz) are gaps or supplier links. The library text layer of Lan's thesis prints the box symbol as the digit 2; all statements involving it were checked on page images.

nodes.title: Discriminant, inverse different and unramified primes of an order (Lan 1.1.1.6-1.1.1.21)
nodes.statement: Let R be a Dedekind domain, A a finite-dimensional separable Frac(R)-algebra with center E, and O an R-order in A, t = [A : Frac(R)]. The discriminant Disc_{O/R} is the ideal of R generated by Det(Tr_{A/Frac(R)}(x_i x_j)) for x_1,...,x_t in O; the inverse different is Diff^{-1}_{O/R} = {x in A : Tr(xy) in R for all y in O}, a two-sided ideal; Disc_{O/R} = Norm(Diff_{O/R}) = [Diff^{-1}_{O/R} : O]_R (Prop. 1.1.1.16). A prime p of R is unramified in O if p does not divide Disc_{O/R} (Def. 1.1.1.18). If Frac(R) is a global field and p does not divide Disc_{O/R}, then (1) O is maximal at p, (2) O tensor R^_p is a product of matrix algebras with center O_E tensor R^_p, and (3) p is unramified in A and in E (Prop. 1.1.1.21).
hypotheses: R Dedekind (for 1.1.1.16 and 1.1.1.21); Frac(R) a global field for Prop. 1.1.1.21
A separable over Frac(R), so the reduced trace pairing is nondegenerate (Lan cites Reiner [107, Thm. 9.26])
O an R-order (subring with the same identity that is a full R-lattice); Lemma 1.1.1.9 needs O locally free over R
proofSteps: Lemma 1.1.1.9: localize so O is free; the trace pairing gives a perfect pairing O x Diff^{-1} -> R with dual bases.
Prop. 1.1.1.16: writing a basis of O in the dual basis of Diff^{-1} shows the Gram matrix of the trace form equals the transition matrix, so Disc = Norm(Diff) = [Diff^{-1} : O].
Prop. 1.1.1.21(1): for orders O in O' one has O in O' in Diff^{-1}_{O'} in Diff^{-1}_{O}; if p does not divide Disc then O tensor R_p = Diff^{-1} tensor R_p, forcing maximality at p.
Prop. 1.1.1.21(2): imported from Reiner [107, Thm. 10.5 and Thm. 25.7] (not read here).
Prop. 1.1.1.21(3): restricting to the center shows p does not divide Disc_{O_E/R}; conclude with Prop. 1.1.1.19 ([107, Thm. 25.3], all maximal orders have the same discriminant) and Def. 1.1.1.20.
acceptance: For O = Z[i] in Q(i), the trace Gram matrix in the basis (1, i) is diag(2, -2), so Disc = (4) and only 2 is ramified.
For the non-maximal order Z[2i], check that 2 divides Disc, consistent with statement (1) of Prop. 1.1.1.21.
For O = M_n(Z) check Disc is the unit ideal, so every prime is unramified.

nodes.title: The determinant polynomial Det_{C|M} classifies modules in every characteristic; the trace does so only in characteristic zero (Lan 1.1.2)
nodes.statement: Let C be a finite-dimensional separable algebra over a field k with center E, K any field extension of k, and alpha_1,...,alpha_t a k-basis of C. For a finitely generated C tensor_k K-module M put Det_{C|M}(X_1,...,X_t) := Det_K(X_1 alpha_1 + ... + X_t alpha_t | M), an element of K[C^vee] = k[C^vee] tensor_k K independent of the basis (Def. 1.1.2.18). Then two finitely generated C tensor_k K-modules are isomorphic if and only if their Det polynomials agree (Prop. 1.1.2.20). If char(k) = 0, two such modules are isomorphic if and only if Tr_K(x|M_1) = Tr_K(x|M_2) for all x in C (Cor. 1.1.2.14); Remark 1.1.2.15 states that char(k) = 0 is used in an essential way. Relative version (Def. 1.1.2.21): for R_0 a noetherian domain, O an R_0-order that is free over R_0, a scheme S over Spec(R_0) and a locally free O_S-module M of finite rank with O-action, Det_{O|M}(X) := Det_{O_S}(X_1 alpha_1 + ... + X_t alpha_t | M) in O_S[O^vee], independent of the free R_0-basis.
hypotheses: k a field, C finite-dimensional and separable over k (so E is a separable commutative k-algebra); K an arbitrary, possibly infinite, field extension
modules finitely generated over C tensor_k K
trace criterion only when char(k) = 0
relative definition: O free as an R_0-module; M locally free of finite rank over O_S
proofSteps: Lemma 1.1.2.1 and Cor. 1.1.2.2: E tensor_k K is a product over Gal(K^sep/K)-orbits [tau] of fields K_[tau], and C tensor_k K is the product of the simple K-algebras C tensor_{E,[tau]} K_[tau].

Lemma 1.1.2.4 (all simple modules of a simple Artinian algebra are isomorphic; Lan cites [63, Lem. 4.3.2]) gives Cor. 1.1.2.6: each factor has a unique simple module W_[tau] and every finitely generated module is a direct sum of W_[tau]^{m_[tau]} with the multiplicities determining it.
Equation (1.1.2.10): W_[tau] tensor_K K^sep is the direct sum over tau' in [tau] of W_{tau'}^{s_[tau]}.

nodes.title: Field of definition of a module over a separable algebra (Lan 1.1.2.7-1.1.2.16)
nodes.statement: In the setting of the previous node, the field of definition K_0 of a finitely generated C tensor_k K-module M_0 is the subfield of K^sep fixed by all sigma in Aut(K^sep/k) such that M_0 tensor_K K^sep is isomorphic to its sigma-twist as a C tensor_k K^sep-module (Def. 1.1.2.7). K_0 lies in K and does not depend on K^sep (Remark 1.1.2.8); it lies in E^Gal intersect K (Cor. 1.1.2.12). If char(k) = 0 then K_0 = k(Tr_K(x|M_0) : x in C) (Cor. 1.1.2.16). Being the field of definition does NOT imply that M_0 descends to a C tensor_k K_0-module (Remark 1.1.2.9).
hypotheses: C finite-dimensional separable over k with center E; K a field extension of k; M_0 finitely generated
trace description only when char(k) = 0
proofSteps: Galois twisting permutes the simple modules W_tau by W_tau tensor_{K^sep,sigma} K^sep = W_{sigma o tau}; M_0 tensor K^sep is sigma-invariant iff s_[tau] m_[tau] = s_[sigma tau] m_[sigma tau] for all tau.
Cor. 1.1.2.11-1.1.2.12: the field of definition of W_tau lies in tau(E), hence K_0 lies in the Galois closure E^Gal.
Cor. 1.1.2.16: in characteristic zero sigma(Tr(x|M_0)) is the trace on the sigma-twist, so by Cor. 1.1.2.14 sigma fixes the isomorphism class iff it fixes all traces.

nodes.title: Multirank classification and residue-field detection of projective O_R-modules at unramified primes (Lan 1.1.3, 1.2.1.21-1.2.1.33)
nodes.statement: (a) Lemma 1.1.3.1: let R_0 be a noetherian domain and O an R_0-order that is projective over R_0; let R be a noetherian local R_0-algebra with residue field k, M_1 a finitely generated O tensor R-module that is projective over O tensor R, and M_2 a finitely generated O tensor R-module projective over R. Then M_1 and M_2 are isomorphic iff they are isomorphic modulo the maximal ideal. (b) Now let R_0 be the ring of integers of a number field, k a field of characteristic 0 or a finite field with R_0 -> k of kernel p, p unramified in O, Lambda = k if p = 0 and the unramified complete extension with residue field k otherwise (W(k) if R_0 = Z), R a noetherian local Lambda-algebra with residue field k. Every finitely generated projective O_R-module is isomorphic to a direct sum of the M_{tau,R}^{m_tau} for uniquely determined integers m_tau >= 0, its O_R-multirank (Lemma 1.1.3.4, Def. 1.1.3.5); being projective over O_R is not the same as being locally free (Remark 1.1.3.2). (c) For R_0 = Z the O-multirank of an O-lattice is the B-multirank of its rationalization (Def. 1.2.1.21); an O tensor R-module is integrable if it is M tensor R for an O-lattice M (Def. 1.2.1.23); under the assumptions of (b) with R_0 = Z, p not dividing Disc and R moreover a noetherian complete local ring with residue field k (the setting stated before Lemma 1.2.1.26), an O_R-module is integrable of O-multirank (m_[tau]) iff it is finitely generated projective of O_R-multirank (m_tau) with m_tau = s_[tau] m_[tau], and this can be checked modulo the maximal ideal (Lemmas 1.2.1.29, 1.2.1.33). (d) Generalized Noether-Skolem (Lemma 1.1.3.6): every C-automorphism of End_{O_F,R}(M) is inner by an invertible element of End_C(M), for M finitely generated projective and C an O_{F,R}-subalgebra containing O_{F,R}.
hypotheses: (a): O projective over R_0; M_1 projective over O tensor R and M_2 projective over R
(b)-(d): R_0 ring of integers of a number field (R_0 = Z in Section 1.2.1); k of characteristic 0 or finite; p = ker(R_0 -> k) unramified in O
(c): R_0 = Z; p does not divide Disc_{O/Z}; R a noetherian complete local ring with residue field k (setting before Lemma 1.2.1.26, printed p. 38); s_[tau] = 1 when p > 0 (Def. 1.2.1.28)
proofSteps: (a): lift a residue isomorphism to a morphism f using projectivity of M_1 over O tensor R; since O is a direct summand of a free R_0-module, both modules are R-projective, so f is an isomorphism by Nakayama.

(b): by Prop. 1.1.1.21 O tensor Lambda is maximal and, for p > 0, a product of matrix algebras M_{d_tau}(O_{F_tau}); by (a) reduce to finite-dimensional modules over a semisimple algebra with separable center, classified by Cor. 1.1.2.6.

(c): Lemma 1.2.1.24 shows the rationalization of an integrable module over a flat R is well defined; Lemma 1.2.1.29 writes M = (M_[Z] tensor Lambda) tensor_Lambda R, where the O_Lambda-lattice M_[Z] tensor Lambda is projective over O_Lambda by Props. 1.1.1.21 and 1.1.1.23 (maximal orders are hereditary, cited to [107, Thm. 21.4 and Cor. 21.5]), and compares multiranks by Lemma 1.2.1.26; Lemma 1.2.1.33 follows from Lemma 1.2.1.29, and its reduction to the residue field from Lemma 1.1.3.1.

(d): twist the E-module structure of M by the automorphism; the twisted module is isomorphic modulo the maximal ideal because the center is separable over k, hence isomorphic by (a); the isomorphism is the inner automorphism.

nodes.title: PEL-type O-lattices, their polarization h, and the similitude group scheme G over Z (Lan 1.2.1.2-1.2.1.9)
nodes.statement: Let B be a finite-dimensional semisimple Q-algebra with involution * that is positive (Tr_{B/Q}(x x*) > 0 for x != 0), with center F, and O a *-stable order in B. Put Z(1) := ker(exp : C -> C^x). A symplectic O-lattice (L, <,>) is an O-lattice L with an alternating pairing L x L -> Z(1) such that <bx, y> = <x, b* y>. A polarization of it is an R-algebra homomorphism h : C -> End_{O tensor R}(L tensor R) with <h(z)x, y> = <x, h(z^c)y> and such that, for each choice of sqrt(-1), (2 pi sqrt(-1))^{-1} <., h(sqrt(-1)).> is symmetric and positive definite; the last condition forces <,> to be nondegenerate (Def. 1.2.1.2). A PEL-type O-lattice (L, <,>, h) is such a triple with R = Z (Def. 1.2.1.3), an integral version of Kottwitz's (B, *, V, <,>, h) (Remark 1.2.1.4). For each Z-algebra R, G(R) = {(g, r) in GL_{O tensor R}(L tensor R) x G_m(R) : <gx, gy> = r<x, y>}, an affine group scheme over Z with similitude character nu(g, r) = r (Def. 1.2.1.6); r is determined by g when L != 0 and R is flat over Z, but G = G_m when L = 0; h is not needed to define G (Remark 1.2.1.7); G need not be smooth over all of Z (Remark 1.2.1.8). The dual lattice is L^# = {x in L tensor Q : <x, y> in Z(1) for all y in L} (Def. 1.1.4.11). Congruence subgroups: Gamma(n) = ker(G(Z) -> G(Z/nZ)), U^box(n) = ker(G(Z^^box) -> G(Z/nZ)) for n prime to the set of primes box, U(n) = ker(G(Z^) -> G(Z/nZ)) (Remark 1.2.1.9). Complex meaning (Lan intro 5.1.1): A_0 = (L tensor R)/L with complex structure h_0 is an abelian variety with polarization A_0 -> (L tensor R)/L^#, O-action satisfying the Rosati condition, and liftable principal level structures.
hypotheses: * positive: Tr_{B/Q}(x x*) > 0 for all nonzero x in B
O a Z-order in B stable under *; L finitely generated and Z-torsion-free with O-action (Lan intro 5.1.1 phrases this as a finitely generated free Z-module)
pairing alternating, O-compatible, valued in Z(1); h satisfies both conditions of Def. 1.2.1.2
Remark 1.2.1.9 requires n prime to box for U^box(n)
proofSteps: Definitions 1.1.4.2, 1.1.4.6-1.1.4.11 (symplectic modules, symplectic morphisms (f, nu(f)) where nu(f) is part of the datum, dual lattice).
Definitions 1.2.1.2, 1.2.1.3 and 1.2.1.6 as stated; Remark 1.2.1.8 notes that for non-flat R the induced pairing need not be nondegenerate.

nodes.title: Abelian schemes, isogenies, quasi-isogenies and Z_(box)^x-isogenies (Lan 1.3.1)
nodes.statement: An abelian scheme is a group scheme A -> S that is proper, smooth, with geometrically connected fibers (Def. 1.3.1.1); it is of finite presentation, so noetherian approximation (Theorem 1.3.1.3, EGA IV-3 Section 8) applies. Rigidity (Prop. 1.3.1.4, Mumford's rigidity lemma) gives: morphisms to separated group schemes of finite presentation agreeing on one fiber over a connected base differ by a section (Cor. 1.3.1.5); pointed maps are homomorphisms (Cor. 1.3.1.6); A is commutative with a unique group structure for a given identity (Cor. 1.3.1.7-1.3.1.8). An isogeny is a surjective homomorphism with quasi-finite kernel; isogenies of smooth group schemes are flat, and of abelian schemes finite flat of finite presentation with locally constant kernel rank (Lemma 1.3.1.11, Cor. 1.3.1.12). For a set box of primes, an isogeny is prime-to-box if its kernel rank is prime-to-box (Def. 1.3.1.15). A quasi-isogeny is an equivalence class of triples (B, g, h) of isogenies g : B -> A, h : B -> A' (Def. 1.3.1.16); it is prime-to-box (a Z_(box)^x-isogeny) if g and h can be chosen prime-to-box (Def. 1.3.1.17); isogenies embed fully faithfully (Lemma 1.3.1.18); Z_(box)^x-isogenies compose by fiber product (Def. 1.3.1.19) and are invertible (Remark 1.3.1.20); over S with finitely many connected components one can take g = [N] with N prime-to-box (Remark 1.3.1.21).
hypotheses: box an arbitrary set of rational primes (possibly empty or infinite)
Lemma 1.3.1.11 is reduced to the noetherian case and quotes EGA IV-3 11.3.10 and 15.4.2 (not read)
proofSteps: Prop. 1.3.1.4 is proved in the source (after Mumford [96, Prop. 6.1]): first over a one-point base by comparing structure sheaves, then by showing the closed locus where f = eta o p contains an open neighbourhood of the fiber and using connectedness.
Cor. 1.3.1.5-1.3.1.8 follow from Prop. 1.3.1.4 by standard manipulations transcribed in the source.
Lemma 1.3.1.11: reduce to S noetherian by Theorem 1.3.1.3 and quote EGA.
acceptance: Check that, for A of positive relative dimension, [N] : A -> A is a Z_(box)^x-isogeny iff N is prime-to-box, and that the notation f = N^{-1}h of Remark 1.3.1.21 means f o [N] = [N] o f = h with h a prime-to-box isogeny (S with finitely many connected components, or N a section of (Z_(box)^x)_S).

nodes.title: Dual abelian scheme, lambda_L, polarizations and Z_(box)^x-polarizations (Lan 1.3.2)
nodes.statement: For an abelian scheme A -> S the rigidified Picard functors Pic_e(A/S) and Pic^0_e(A/S) are representable, and Pic^0_e(A/S) is represented by an abelian scheme A^vee (Theorem 1.3.2.3, quoted from Faltings-Chai [42, Ch. I, Section 1]; representability under local projectivity also follows from Hilbert schemes, Remark 1.3.2.4). A rigidified L gives lambda_L : A -> A^vee via D_2(L) = m*L tensor pr_1*L^{-1} tensor pr_2*L^{-1} (Construction 1.3.2.7); lambda_L is symmetric (Lemma 1.3.2.13); A -> (A^vee)^vee is an isomorphism (Lemma 1.3.2.8); dual isogenies have the same rank (Lemma 1.3.2.11). Etale locally every symmetric homomorphism A -> A^vee is some lambda_L (Prop. 1.3.2.14). For symmetric lambda the conditions (1) over each geometric point s of S, lambda_s is lambda_L for some ample invertible sheaf L over A_s, (2) etale locally lambda = lambda_L with L relatively ample, (3) (Id, lambda)*P_A relatively ample, are equivalent (Prop. 1.3.2.15); a polarization is a symmetric lambda satisfying them, principal if an isomorphism, prime-to-box if a prime-to-box isogeny (Def. 1.3.2.16). A Z_(box)^x-polarization is a Z_(box)^x-isogeny lambda : A -> A^vee with [N] o lambda a polarization for some locally constant positive integer N, not necessarily prime-to-box (Def. 1.3.2.19); f^vee o lambda o f and lambda^{-1} are again Z_(box)^x-polarizations (Cor. 1.3.2.21).

nodes.title: Prime-to-box Tate modules and the lattice description of Z_(box)^x-isogeny classes (Lan 1.3.5)
nodes.statement: For a Delta-divisible commutative group G, V_Delta(G) and T_Delta(G) are defined by compatible divisible sequences (Def. 1.3.5.1); for box a set of primes, V^box and T^box use Delta = Z_(box)^x intersect Z_>0, with exact sequence 0 -> T^box A -> V^box A -> A^box_tors -> 0 for an abelian variety over an algebraically closed field whose characteristic lies in box if positive. Lemma 1.3.5.2: for (A, lambda, i) over such a field, equivalence classes of Z_(box)^x-isogenies f : (A, lambda, i) -> (A', lambda', i') correspond to open compact subgroups of V^box A via f -> V(f)^{-1}(T^box A'); O-invariant subgroups correspond to those with i' an O-structure. Prop. 1.3.5.3: for S connected locally noetherian with geometric point s, commutative finite etale group schemes over S are equivalent to finite continuous pi_1(S, s)-modules. Cor. 1.3.5.4: for S connected locally noetherian with residue characteristics 0 or in box, Z_(box)^x-isogeny classes out of (A, lambda, i) correspond to pi_1(S, s)-invariant open compact subgroups of V^box A_s, and O-invariant ones to targets with an O-structure. Remark 1.3.5.5: if lambda is not prime-to-box, no member of the class has a prime-to-box polarization.

nodes.title: Principal level-n structures as symplectic-liftable O-equivariant isomorphisms (alpha_n, nu_n) (Lan 1.3.6)
nodes.statement: Let (A, lambda, i) be an abelian scheme over a scheme S over Z_(box) with a prime-to-box polarization and an O-structure, and n >= 1 prime-to-box. An O-equivariant symplectic isomorphism (L/nL)_S -> A[n] is a pair (alpha_n, nu_n) of an O-equivariant isomorphism alpha_n : (L/nL)_S -> A[n] and nu_n : ((Z/nZ)(1))_S -> mu_{n,S} intertwining <,> with the lambda-Weil pairing e^lambda (Def. 1.3.6.1). Because L need not be self-dual, the induced pairing on L/nL may be degenerate or trivial and O-equivariance may be undetectable mod n, so an integral principal level-n structure of type (L tensor Z^^box, <,>) is required to be symplectic-liftable: there is a tower (S_m -> S) over n | m, m prime-to-box, of finite etale coverings with S_n = S, compatible O-equivariant symplectic isomorphisms (alpha_m, nu_m) over S_m reducing to (alpha_l, nu_l) (Def. 1.3.6.2). Lan states that nu_n is uniquely determined by alpha_n if L != 0 and is the essential information if L = 0, and suppresses nu_n from notation. Liftability is nontrivial even for n = 1 and forces ker(lambda) to be isomorphic to ((L^# tensor Z^^box)/(L tensor Z^^box))_S (Remark 1.3.6.3). A level structure lifts at every geometric point to an O tensor Z^^box-equivariant symplectic isomorphism (alpha^, nu^) : L tensor Z^^box -> T^box A_s (Lemma 1.3.6.5); over locally noetherian S, liftability holds iff it holds at every geometric point, and iff at one geometric point of each connected component (Lemma 1.3.6.6, Cor. 1.3.6.7).

lambda prime-to-box polarization, i an O-structure satisfying the Rosati condition

Lemma 1.3.6.6: on a connected component, the U^box(n)-orbit of a lift alpha^ is pi_1-invariant because A[n] and mu_n are locally constant, giving pi_1(S, s) -> U^box(n); preimages of U^box(m) define the finite etale covers S_m, and Prop. 1.3.5.3 converts the pi_1-equivariant isomorphisms back to isomorphisms of group schemes over S_m.

The claim that nu_n is determined by alpha_n when L != 0 is stated inside Def. 1.3.6.2 without proof. Lan's survey (intro 5.1.1, after (5.1.1.11)) says nu_{0,n} is not determined by alpha_{0,n} when <,> is not perfect modulo n; that is true of the defining diagram alone (compare Lan Def. 1.2.1.6: r is determined by g only when L != {0} and R is flat over Z, and Z/nZ is not flat; Remark 1.1.4.9). nodes.title: Rational level-H structures based at a geometric point, base-point independence, and comparison with integral level structures (Lan 1.3.8)
nodes.statement: Let S be locally noetherian over Z_(box), s a geometric point, (A, lambda, i) with lambda a Z_(box)^x-polarization and i an O tensor Z_(box)-structure. The four library sources the packet names (Lan thesis revision, Lan intro, Milne, Hida) were fetched from the author sites. Their SHA-256 hashes match the packet. Faltings 1983 is public on GDZ (different scan, same printed pages). Lan's public thesis and book errata were used to check that the nodes follow the corrected statements. The proof summary (printed p. 51) has no sign condition. The node now follows the proof, and a gap and source issue are recorded; neither errata list has it. (3) Faltings Satz 1 counts semiabelian models over Spec(R) with principal polarization and h(A) <= c, and A_g there is the coarse moduli scheme. The 'same bad reduction' step is also unproved and relies on semistability. The M6 node misdescribed all three, and its twist test over Q was out of scope.
